**Inspection record**

*Directly observed — image A (384×384 PNG):* one flat, saturated red circle on a plain white background, centred horizontally and slightly above middle. Black sans-serif marker "A17" printed below it.

*Directly observed — image B (384×384 PNG):* one flat, saturated blue square (sharp corners, equal sides) on the same plain white background, positioned in the same central area. Black sans-serif marker "B28" printed below it in the same location and style as A's label.

*Comparison:* Same canvas size, same white background, same label placement and typography, and comparably large single flat-colour shapes. Differences: shape (circle vs. square), colour (red vs. blue), and label text ("A17" vs. "B28").

*Uncertainty:* I judged colour and shape visually, without sampling pixel values; exact RGB codes, font, and precise dimensions/placement offsets are not verified. The reported 384×384 size and PNG format come from the tool metadata; original file bytes may differ from the normalized copy. The hashes listed in metadata (A begins c1b1e6…, B begins 4cb998…) identify the files but were not independently verified.

*How to tell them apart:* Trust the printed markers — "A17" = red circle, "B28" = blue square. Failing that, colour is unambiguous at a glance; shape distinguishes them even to a colour-blind viewer, and differing file hashes confirm they are distinct files. Filenames were not used as evidence for either item's contents.
